comments.postCaption: Some people experience a powerful wave of chills, goosebumps, or tingling sensations while listening to certain songs. This response is known as frisson, a real psychological phenomenon that occurs when music strongly activates the brain’s emotional and reward systems. Researchers believe frisson is linked to the release of dopamine, a chemical involved in pleasure, motivation, and anticipation. Unexpected chord changes, emotional lyrics, soaring vocals, or dramatic musical buildups can all increase the chances of experiencing it. Not everyone experiences frisson, and those who do may feel it more often during music that has personal meaning or evokes strong emotions. Scientists also believe people who are more open to new experiences are generally more likely to experience these musical chills. wizdomlezz special people button❤️—> xo_whit_xo I also get choked up and cry. even to upbeat fun songs just because I love it so much its_mamta_007 😍❤️❤️🙌 llinett77 Scientifically the reason
